title: Urgency and Foreseeability Risk
learning_objectives: Distinguish genuine urgency from poor planning
red_flags: Foreseeable recurring needs treated as urgent

n1.text: A department requests an urgent procurement citing an immediate operational need, but the supplies are regularly consumed.
n1.challenge: How should you process this request?

A.text: Review the planning timeline to check if the need was foreseeable.
A.feedback: Good. Checking foreseeability establishes whether genuine urgency exists.

B.text: Process immediately as an urgent procedure to ensure continuity.
B.feedback: Processing without review risks an audit finding for poor planning.
B.expert_log: Processed urgent request without verifying foreseeability.

C.text: Reject the request and require standard procedure, halting operations.
C.feedback: Halting operations entirely without investigating alternative coverage harms the public body.
C.expert_log: Halted operations rather than investigating bridge contracts.

n2.text: The timeline shows the need was foreseeable, but failure to act will now cause severe operational disruption.
n2.challenge: How to proceed while minimizing risk?

A.text: Document the planning failure and escalate for a minimal bridging contract while launching standard procedure.
A.feedback: Excellent. A bridging contract ensures continuity while minimizing audit risk.
A.expert_log: Initiated bridging contract and documented planning failure.

B.text: Approve the full urgent procedure due to the severe disruption risk.
B.feedback: Approving full urgency for foreseeable needs is a high audit risk.
B.expert_log: Approved full urgent procedure despite foreseeability.

C.text: Request the department to alter the dates on their memo to hide the delay.
C.feedback: Altering documents creates severe audit concern and requires further review.

n3.text: The urgent procedure is challenged by an auditor noting the supplies are regular consumables.

A.text: Provide a detailed justification linking the specific delayed delivery to unforeseeable external events.
A.feedback: Strong documentation of external unforeseeable factors mitigates risk.
A.expert_log: Defended urgency with external unforeseeable event documentation.

B.text: Argue that operational necessity overrides procedural requirements.
B.feedback: Operational necessity alone does not justify circumventing standard procedures if foreseeable.
B.expert_log: Used weak audit defensibility against audit finding.

C.text: Withdraw the award and cancel the procurement.
C.feedback: Canceling late causes disruption and administrative chaos.
C.expert_log: Canceled procurement reactively after audit challenge.
